headline: Your Indico Data waterfall journey.
subheadline: A scrollable GTMx strategy artifact for routing P&C carriers, MGAs, and reinsurers into the right Indico intake-and-orchestration offer. List building, campaign angles, and sample copy, prepared for Caroline Hsu.
productSummary: Indico Data (indicodata.ai) is the Intake & Orchestration Platform for insurance operations. Tagline: Keep insurance work in motion. It ingests, enriches, and orchestrates unstructured work (submissions, claims, servicing) into downstream-ready data. Homepage workflows: Underwriting (submission to system-ready work in minutes), Claims (FNOL through resolution), Mid-Term Adjustments (inbox to action), Broker Reconciliation (system-ready remittances). Positioning: purpose-built for insurance, not generic OCR/IDP/workflow tools; handles loss runs, SOVs, ACORDs, emails, and attachments. Platform (indicodata.ai/platform): Agentic AI for insurance operations; Agent Gallery / Agent Studio / Agentic Workflow Canvas; SOC 2, encryption, RBAC, audit logs; not generic LLM output. Ingest / Enrich / Orchestrate agents. Homepage metrics (reconfirmed 2026-09-02): <30 sec SOV & loss run processing; 90% faster cycle time; 4x increase in processing capacity. Case-study tiles: 85% submission processing time (links to leading US commercial P&C insurer story); +$30M quarterly premium growth (Markel); <30 sec SOV & loss run (Convex); 40% processing costs (Cognizant — mortgage title/deed, not insurance). Named on-site: Convex Insurance (Andrea Read, Head of Technology Engineering: reduced time spent on SOVs by over 90%; median SOV/loss-run processing from hours to under 30 seconds); Markel (F500 specialty, +$30M underwriting premiums per quarter, up to 1,200 submissions/day without adding headcount; claims FNOL 48% faster claim setup and 33% lower ingestion costs upstream of Guidewire ClaimCenter); Allstate (underwriting/renewal review from 7 days to under 15 minutes); Kashif Syed, CIO, HDI Global US (complex submissions captured, validated, moved); unnamed F500 Sr. Director Claims Transformation (FNOL quality and speed); unnamed Top 10 global carrier CTO (why-indico: net written premium +50% without expanding the team). About: CEO Tom Wilde; 2025 surpasses support of over $50B in GWP. IDP page names core-system handoff into Guidewire, Duck Creek, and Sapiens. Why-indico: insurance-native intake, not generic AI / legacy IDP; Gartner Hype Cycle for P&C Insurance 2025 (digital underwriting and IDP). Sells to carriers, MGAs, and reinsurers — insurance vertical only.
coreInsight: Caroline already sells an insurance-native Intake & Orchestration Platform so carriers, MGAs, and reinsurers stop stalling submissions, FNOL, MTAs, and remittances in inboxes and generic OCR/IDP tools. The one list is insurance-vertical only: P&C carriers, MGAs, reinsurers, Lloyd's managing agents, and specialty insurers with underwriting, claims, or servicing operations — not banks, mortgage processors, healthcare, or generic enterprise IDP buyers. The one routing signal is intake_stack_state: how unstructured insurance work already shows up, because BuiltWith plus a LinkedIn jobs pull plus a homepage/careers/broker-portal scrape returns a named generic IDP/OCR/intake competitor, open hiring for submission/FNOL/intake ops, live SOV/FNOL/submission language, or none of those, in one cheap pass. Buyer title (CIO, Head of Underwriting Ops, Chief Claims Officer) and segment (carrier vs MGA vs reinsurer) are merge tags after the account is routed. They are not a second waterfall.

sections.label: Signal
sections.title: The signal is how unstructured insurance work already shows up
sections.takeaway: BuiltWith plus a LinkedIn jobs pull plus a homepage/careers/broker-portal scrape already names a generic IDP/OCR/intake competitor, open hiring for submission or FNOL intake, live SOV/FNOL/submission language, or none of those. That stack-state is stronger than a title guess, and it is cheap to collect.

sections.label: Waterfall
sections.title: One cascade routes every in-TAM carrier, MGA, and reinsurer
sections.takeaway: First match wins. Named generic IDP/OCR tools go first, then open intake/FNOL hiring, then visible SOV/FNOL/submission language, then every remaining in-TAM insurance operations account.

sections.label: Tiers
sections.title: Each intake state gets a different first offer
sections.takeaway: Generic IDP on stack gets an Insurance IDP Switch Brief. Intake hiring gets an Intake Capacity Brief. Live SOV/FNOL/submission language gets a Front-Door Intake Brief. The rest get the Keep-Work-in-Motion Playbook.

sections.label: Campaigns
sections.title: Switch the generic IDP, stop hiring for inbox work, fix the front door, then cover the rest
sections.takeaway: The list is always in-TAM insurance operations — P&C carriers, MGAs, reinsurers — aimed at CIOs, Heads of Underwriting Ops, Chief Claims Officers, and transformation leaders. Segment (carrier vs MGA) is a merge tag, not a second TAM. A/Bs sit on the exclusive routes.

sections.label: Email Copy
sections.title: Copy that names the intake state already on their stack
sections.takeaway: Notice the competitor, the intake job posts, or the SOV/FNOL language, poke the inbox-stall that state implies, then ask for a one-letter Y.

sections.label: Launch
sections.title: Launch the generic-IDP route first
sections.takeaway: Start where they already pay Hyperscience, ABBYY, UiPath, Kofax, or a peer and still leak insurance-specific SOV, loss-run, and FNOL intake. Prove reply density, then roll intake-hiring accounts, SOV/FNOL-language accounts, and the remaining-TAM catch-all.

signalReasons: Apollo plus LinkedIn plus AM Best / NAIC / AAMGA / Lloyd's directories are the TAM Caroline already sells into: P&C carriers, MGAs, reinsurers, and specialty insurers with underwriting, claims, or servicing operations — insurance-vertical only, not mortgage, banking, or generic enterprise IDP. TAM account count is not published on indicodata.ai; treat size as unknown and keep each launch tier ≥~1,500 contacts.

The same BuiltWith / script scan plus LinkedIn jobs pull plus homepage/careers/broker-portal scrape returns intake_stack_state: a named generic IDP/OCR/intake tool (Hyperscience, ABBYY, UiPath Document Understanding, Kofax, IBM Datacap, and peers), open hiring for submission/FNOL/intake ops, or live SOV/FNOL/submission language — enough to route without a second expensive enrichment product.

The ladder maps to live Indico positioning on indicodata.ai: purpose-built vs generic OCR, IDP, and workflow tools that break on loss runs, SOVs, ACORDs, emails, and attachments; ingest / enrich / orchestrate into Guidewire, Duck Creek, or Sapiens; homepage <30 sec SOV & loss run, 90% faster cycle time, 4x processing capacity; Markel +$30M quarterly premium; Convex 90%+ SOV time reduction.
Segment (carrier vs MGA vs reinsurer) and buyer title are scrape filters and merge tags. They are not a second waterfall. Apollo is email last after the domain is routed, never the TAM spine alone.

routingRules.why: Already a customer. Named case-study accounts on indicodata.ai (Convex, Markel, Allstate, HDI Global US) are not enough to exclude every subsidiary or MGAs writing on those paper.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND intake_stack_state = competitor_idp (Hyperscience, ABBYY, UiPath Document Understanding, Kofax, IBM Datacap, or another named generic OCR / IDP / document-automation tool on BuiltWith / site)
routingRules.why: They already pay for document processing. Strongest intent for Indico's purpose-built pitch: homepage says generic OCR, IDP, and workflow tools break on loss runs, SOVs, ACORDs, emails, and attachments. Convex dropped median SOV and loss-run processing from hours to under 30 seconds.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND hiring_signal = intake_hiring (open LinkedIn / careers roles for submission intake, FNOL / claims intake, document processing, or underwriting assistants doing inbox work; no named competitor IDP)
routingRules.why: They are buying headcount to do the work Indico automates. Maps to homepage 4x processing capacity and Markel: up to 1,200 submissions/day without adding headcount and +$30M underwriting premiums per quarter.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND intake_language = sov_fnol_submission (homepage, careers, broker portal, or FNOL page talks SOVs, loss runs, ACORDs, FNOL, submissions, MTAs, or remittances; no named competitor; no intake hiring)
routingRules.why: The work is publicly live but there is no visible intake layer. Maps to Allstate: document review from 7 days to under 15 minutes.

routingRules.if: in_tam AND none of the above
routingRules.why: Still in TAM (P&C carriers, MGAs, reinsurers). Softest CTA. Mandatory 100% coverage.

tiers.name: Tier 1
tiers.label: Generic IDP / OCR already on the stack
tiers.trigger: BuiltWith or site shows Hyperscience, ABBYY, UiPath Document Understanding, Kofax, IBM Datacap, or another named generic OCR / IDP / document-automation tool
tiers.pain: They already pay for document processing, but a generalist OCR/IDP stack does not unbundle multi-file broker packets or survive SOV / loss-run / ACORD variability.
tiers.valueProp: Indico is purpose-built intake and orchestration for insurance. Homepage: <30 sec SOV & loss run processing, 90% faster cycle time. Convex: median SOV/loss-run processing from hours to under 30 seconds.
tiers.replyDensity: Highest - they already pay for IDP or OCR tooling
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; not published on indicodata.ai — keep each tier ≥~1,500 contacts before launch

tiers.name: Tier 2
tiers.label: Hiring for submission / FNOL / intake ops
tiers.trigger: Open LinkedIn or careers roles for submission intake, FNOL / claims intake, document processors, or underwriting assistants doing inbox work, and no named competitor IDP
tiers.pain: They are scaling the front door with headcount. Every new submission or FNOL wave means more analysts opening emails, unbundling attachments, and rekeying into the core.
tiers.valueProp: Homepage: 4x increase in processing capacity. Markel: process up to 1,200 submissions per day without adding headcount and +$30M underwriting premiums per quarter.
tiers.replyDensity: High - they are already budgeting people against the intake queue

tiers.name: Tier 3
tiers.label: Live SOV / FNOL / submission language, no named IDP
tiers.trigger: Homepage, careers, broker portal, or FNOL page talks SOVs, loss runs, ACORDs, FNOL, submissions, mid-term adjustments, or remittances; in-TAM insurance operations; no named competitor; no intake hiring
tiers.pain: The work is on the public site but intake still stalls in inboxes before it hits the core.
tiers.valueProp: Extraction agents unbundle submissions and claims from emails, attachments, SOVs, and loss runs. Allstate: underwriting and renewal document review from 7 days to under 15 minutes.

tiers.name: Catch-all
tiers.label: Remaining in-TAM carriers / MGAs / reinsurers
tiers.trigger: In-TAM P&C carrier, MGA, reinsurer, or specialty insurer with an operations / underwriting / claims / technology decision maker and no Tier 1-3 intake_stack_state
tiers.pain: Underwriting, claims, and servicing work still stalls in inboxes, and there is no insurance-native intake layer yet.
tiers.valueProp: One intake and orchestration layer across underwriting, claims, mid-term adjustments, and broker reconciliation. Homepage: Keep insurance work in motion; 90% faster cycle time; 4x processing capacity.
tiers.dataSource: Apollo + LinkedIn company + title graph after in_tam gate
tiers.accounts: est. flagged; catch-all must cover remaining TAM
